avalancheActivity.comment:
In steep rocky terrain and on extremely steep slopes small and medium sized avalanches are to be expected as the day progresses. Above approximately 2300 m they can be triggered in the new snow and wind slab layers and reach large size in some cases. Individual gliding avalanches can also occur.

The wind slabs of the last few days can be released by a single winter sport participant in isolated cases in particular on very steep northeast, east and south facing slopes at high altitude. They will be covered with new snow and therefore difficult to recognise. Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls and at the base of rock walls the likelihood of avalanches is higher.

snowpackStructure.comment:
20 to 30 cm of snow will fall until Wednesday above approximately 1200 m.
As a consequence of new snow and a sometimes moderate southeasterly wind, soft wind slabs will form by the evening adjacent to ridgelines.
As a consequence of the occasionally strong northwesterly wind, snow drift accumulations formed at the weekend.
Above approximately 2200 m there are 60 to 130 cm of snow, and even as much as 190 cm in some localities, especially above approximately 2500 m.
The snowpack will be in some cases unstable. Towards its base, the snowpack is moist, in particular below approximately 2500 m.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field.

tendency.highlights: Northerly wind. The danger will persist.

avalancheActivity.comment:
Natural avalanches are possible as the day progresses. Mostly these are small. Above approximately 2300 m they can be released in the new snow and wind slab layers.

The wind slabs of the weekend will be covered with new snow and therefore difficult to recognise. Single backcountry tourers can release avalanches in isolated cases.
Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls and at the base of rock walls the likelihood of avalanches is higher.

snowpackStructure.comment:
10 to 20 cm of snow, and up to 30 cm in some localities, will fall until the evening above approximately 1000 m.
As a consequence of the moderate to strong southeasterly wind, fresh snow drift accumulations will form in the course of the day.
Above approximately 2000 m there are 30 to 60 cm of snow, and even more in some localities.
The snowpack will become in some cases unstable.
Towards its base, the snowpack is moist, in particular below approximately 2500 m.
At low and intermediate altitudes only a little snow is lying.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field.

tendency.highlights: Northerly wind. The danger will persist.
